openings.claim: Locating before clamping may improve captive-joint return. The tighter-fit reversal could reflect premature frictional locking; unmeasured. Replace overall tightness as locating dependency with two adjacent rod faces and an insertion stop.
openings.discriminator: Rival: rod size or compliance dominates regardless of seating order. At equal final restraint, explicit seating should reduce exchange error, including the 18 mm replacement, without increased loaded drift. Similar return distributions defeat the seating explanation; improved unloaded return with excessive loaded drift defeats the joint.
openings.probe: Use four plywood pieces for two fixed L nests and two for independently moving jaws. Cord retains jaws, nuts and loops. Seat each rod against corner and stop before hand tightening. Compare this with tightening without prescribed seating, using one assembly and two operating configurations. Per configuration: twelve exchanges, four ten-second 10 N load trials; exchange each original rod five times, then replace the smaller rod with 18 mm for its final two exchanges. Log exchange time and unloaded/loaded target position; record deviations. Require return within 2 mm and retention there under load, exchanges under forty seconds, 90 mm cube envelope, hand-only assembly/adjustment, plywood-only drilling, no rod drilling/adhesive/permanent marks, and no free-falling components in either configuration.
openings.uncertainty: Unspecified bolt lengths/attachment geometry may prevent captive jaw travel inside the cube. Hardware must furnish stops and rigid nest connections: establish actual layout before fabrication. Plywood stiffness/hand tightening may miss the loaded 2 mm target. Completing fabrication in 100 minutes and comparison in 20 minutes remains unverified.

lineage.reason: Preserves causal relation, rival, both defeats, probe, uncertain fit and feasibility caveats.

decision: Bounded mechanism probe only. Proceed only after physical layout supports separate captive locating/clamping with six 80×40×6 mm plywood pieces, eight M5 bolts/nuts, four washers, two 150 mm elastic loops and 0.5 m cord. Otherwise infeasible; exchange caps do not resolve layout.
